entry.title: Connected by Design: Run Integrated Business Processes, Out of the Box
entry.content:
Running a business well depends on connected processes working together across the organization. A customer opportunity can flow seamlessly through to revenue recognition, a purchase request can move smoothly through to supplier payment, and a workforce plan can connect a hiring decision to a productive employee. Finance and human resources (HR) shape many of these outcomes, giving both functions a unique opportunity to turn connected processes and data into better decisions for the entire business.

 

The strategic question Finance and HR can answer together

Finance and HR often approach the same business opportunity from two complementary angles. Finance brings a cost and capacity lens: how licensing, integration, and infrastructure decisions translate into what the organization can actually execute on. HR brings a focus on agility and the ability to launch initiatives like a new onboarding cycle as the business requires. Bringing those perspectives together opens up a better question: What becomes possible when Finance and HR work from a real-time, intelligent view of the business?

Each system reflected the priorities, requirements, and possibilities of the moment in which it was selected. As the business evolved, those individual choices created an opportunity to bring together what had previously been managed separately. It's no longer a question of whether each system works on its own, but how Finance and HR can build on those investments to create a shared foundation for the decisions they increasingly need to make together.

 

When Finance and HR work from the same context

The organizations leading this shift tend to have one thing in common. They're organizing workforce strategy around a single source of insight rather than around separate functional perspectives. When those workflows connect, the data they produce isn't Finance's version and HR's version sitting side by side. It's one shared picture, built on the same definitions from the start. Connected workflows give Finance and HR the context to evaluate priorities, respond to change, and give leaders a stronger basis for timely, confident decisions.

That shared approach turns integration into everyday business value. Workforce planning becomes a continuous exchange between Finance and HR, while scenario modeling gives CFOs and CHROs something they can act on, not just present. Compliance becomes easier to manage, and smoother handoffs across hiring, onboarding, and budgeting help the organization move forward with greater speed and confidence.

The result is a different kind of conversation. Finance and HR can spend less time establishing context and more time evaluating options, setting priorities, and acting together. Alignment becomes the starting point rather than the outcome.

 

How SAP-managed public cloud ERP turns connection into business value

Across our customer conversations, one thing kept coming up: customers want to focus on business outcomes from day one, with the applications and integrations ready to support them.

SAP-managed public cloud ERP provides that foundation, connecting business processes and data so that teams can work efficiently across functions and turn shared insight into coordinated action. When a customer selects a business scenario like Workforce Management, the integration comes out of the box. SAP provisions all required applications and integration in one guided experience, keeping technical decisions to a minimum and taking care of monitoring and operations. Customers and partners implement the full scenario together, and partners go straight to business design and the outcomes that matter most to customers. Workforce Management (SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central) and Operational Procurement (SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing) are both running in Early Adopter phase now. The next scenario is Opportunity to Order (SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and SAP Sales Cloud V2).

The SAP-managed public cloud ERP community is where you can get the full picture on the latest scenarios, the Early Adopter Care program, as well as blog posts, webinars, and opportunities to learn from customers and partners making the same shift. Connect with us there to ask questions and explore how to get involved or find more under the tag "SAP-managed Public Cloud ERP". If this post sparked a question or an idea, continue the conversation in the comments.

entry.title: Solution order billing with solution bundle
entry.content:
Introduction

When selling bundled solutions — a set of products and services packaged together – sometimes solution bundles are sold with an aggregated price and individual subitems are not priced separately for the end customer. Sometimes it could be that the solution bundle is sold without providing information about the subitems.  There could be other scenarios too. The billing document should also keep the information displayed consistent to the selling and show the structure in the same way.

Solution Order in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition natively supports solution bundles, where a main bundle product contains multiple sub-items — subscription products, professional services, and support contracts. However, to surface this bundle hierarchy on the billing document, a few configuration and extensibility steps are required.

This blog walks you through an approach to achieve that.

Solution Bundle

You will find more information about the solution bundle topic in the following places:

  • Blog: Advanced-solution-bundling-for-solution-order-management-in-sap-s-4hana
  • SAP Help: Bundle Items in Solution Orders

 

Example of billing document with solution bundle

The sample billing document is the example we use in this blog. Each bundle appears as a main line item, with its sub-items grouped and indented beneath it — giving the customer a clear, structured view of what they are being billed for. Note that here we do not want to show the net value for the subitems.

Achieving this output requires a couple of custom fields, BAdI logic, form template enhancement and a couple of configuration settings to be set up.

Configuration Overview

#

Step

1

Create custom fields on the Billing Document Item

2

Create BAdI implementation to populate the custom fields

3

Assign the BAdI implementation to billing document creation process

4

Configure addition of Solution Bundle in Margin Analysis (if needed)

5

Enable generation of a single bill for Solution Order

6

Configure grouping by Solution Bundle for Output

7

Create custom form for adjusting aggregation for Solution Bundle in Output

 

Step 1: Create custom fields on the Billing Document Item

The billing document item must be extended with three custom fields to carry bundle metadata from the originating solution order.

App: Custom Fields and Logic (F1481)

Custom Logic app or Custom Logic tab within Custom Fields and Logic app

Create the following three fields. For each, set Business Context = Billing: Billing Document Item.

Field Technical Name

Label

Type

YY1_BUNDLEITEMNUM_BDI

Bundle Item Number

Text (6)

YY1_BUNDLEPRODID_BDI

Bundle Product ID

Text (40)

YY1_BUNDLEPRODDESC_BDI

Bundle Product Description

Text (40)

 

For each field, before publishing:

1.1  In the UIs and Reports tab, enable the form template SDBIL_CI_PROF_SRV_XX. (XX denotes the language key DE, EN …)

1.2  Save and Publish.

These three fields form the foundation for everything that follows. They will hold the bundle product ID, the bundle item number, and the bundle product description at the billing item level.

Step 2: Create BAdI implementation to populate the custom fields

The custom fields need to be filled automatically whenever a billing document is created from a solution order. This is handled through a BAdI (Business Add-In).

App: Custom Fields and Logic (F1481) → Custom Logic tab

  • Business Context: Sales: Billing Document Item
  • BAdI Description: Custom Data Transfer for Billing Documents(SD_BIL_DATA_TRANSFER)
  • Implementation Description: Fill Bundle Details & Control SO Invoice Split

 

The BAdI implementation does two things:

2.1  Populates the custom fields representing solution bundle info — for each billing item originating from a solution order, it reads BusSolnOrdItemBundleProduct and BusSolnOrdItemBundleItem from the CDS view I_BusSolutionOrderItemEnhcd, then fetches the product description from I_ProductText. These values are written into the three YY1_ fields on the billing item. These fields are used in the custom form for print.

2.2  Controls the invoice split — it clears documentreferenceid and purchaseorderbycustomer at the header level when solution order items are present, ensuring bundle items are consolidated onto a single billing document rather than split.

   ```abap

    MOVE-CORRESPONDING bil_doc TO bil_doc_res.

    MOVE-CORRESPONDING bil_doc_item TO bil_doc_item_res.

    MOVE-CORRESPONDING bil_doc_item_contr TO bil_doc_item_contr_res.

 

    READ TABLE bil_doc_item TRANSPORTING NO FIELDS WITH KEY businesssolutionorder IS NOT INITIAL.

    IF sy-subrc = 0.

      CLEAR bil_doc_res-documentreferenceid.

      CLEAR bil_doc_res-purchaseorderbycustomer.

    ENDIF.

 

    LOOP AT bil_doc_item_res ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_item_res>).

      READ TABLE bil_doc_item ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_item_orig>) WITH KEY billingdocumentitem = <fs_item_res>-billingdocumentitem.

      IF sy-subrc <> 0. CONTINUE. ENDIF.

 

      SELECT SINGLE BusSolnOrdItemBundleProduct, BusSolnOrdItemBundleItem

        FROM I_BusSolutionOrderItemEnhcd

        WHERE BusinessSolutionOrder = @<fs_item_orig>-businesssolutionorder

          AND BusinessSolutionOrderItem = @<fs_item_orig>-businesssolutionorderitem

        INTO @DATA(ls_bundle_info).

 

      IF sy-subrc = 0.

        <fs_item_res>-yy1_bundleprodid_bdi    = ls_bundle_info-BusSolnOrdItemBundleProduct.

        <fs_item_res>-yy1_bundleitemnum_bdi   = ls_bundle_info-BusSolnOrdItemBundleItem.

 

        SELECT SINGLE ProductDescription FROM I_ProductText

          WHERE Product = @LS_bundle_info-BusSolnOrdItemBundleProduct AND Language = @SY-langu

          INTO @<fs_item_res>-yy1_bundleproddesc_bdi.

      ENDIF.

    ENDLOOP.

    ```

Make a note of the Implementation ID generated (e.g., YY1_SOMEBADIIMPLEMENTATIONID) — it is needed in the next step. Publish the logic after saving.

Step 3: Assign the BAdI implementation to billing document creation process

The BAdI from Step 2 must be triggered every time a billing document is created. This is done by defining a custom copy routine and assigning it in copy control.

3.1  Define the Custom Routine

App: Manage Your Solution → SSCUI 102865 (Define Custom Data Transfer Routines for Billing Documents)

3.1.1  Create a New Entry.

3.1.2  Enter a Routine Number from the custom range, e.g., 3000001.

3.1.3  Enter the BAdI Implementation ID from Step 2.

3.1.4  Save.

3.2  Assign the Routine in Copy Control

App: Manage Your Solution → SSCUIs 102762,102763 and 102764 for copy controls for billing documents

3.2.1  Open the relevant copy control relationship (e.g., Delivery Document  to Billing Document or Billing to Billing).

3.2.2  Navigate to the Item level.

3.2.3  For each relevant Item Category, locate the field `Custom data Transfer `.

3.2.4  Replace the existing routine number with your new custom routine number (e.g., 3000001).

3.2.5  Save.

From this point on, every billing document created for items with the assigned category will execute the BAdI and populate the solution bundle fields.

Step 4: Configure addition of Solution Bundle in Margin Analysis

If you want to also report on the solution bundle then you can enable the custom fields created for accounting too:

4.1  In the Business Scenarios tab for each of the custom fields, enable Sales: Billing Document to Accounting: Journal Entry Integration. Save and publish.

4.2  Follow the blog Enable-profitability-reporting-for-bundle-in-solution-order-management for the custom fields.

Step 5: Enable generation of a single bill for Solution Order

Make use of blog Collective-billing-of-solution-order-include-prof-serv-project-and-other-docs-into-single-invoice to bring together all billing items from solution order and the solution bundle together on a single invoice, if you have a customer project in the solution order or the solution bundle.

Step 6: Configure grouping by Solution Bundle for Output

The billing output form must be enhanced to include the custom bundle fields so they appear on the printed or PDF document. Here, the form template for professional services billing document is reused. With this, the aggregate rule configuration for grouping was used.  This makes it possible to group the items by bundle product and bundle item without modifications required for the form.

There may be an alternative approach with the standard billing document template too that you may want to explore.

6.1  Configure Flexible Billing Output Aggregation

This is the step that produces the hierarchical display in the billing output — grouping sub-items visually beneath their parent bundle, exactly as shown in the sample invoice.

6.2  Define the Aggregation Rule

App: Manage Your Solution → SSCUI 103967 (Define Rules for Flexible Billing Output Aggregation – PS)

Create a Rule with the following Group Items aggregation levels(eg 9):

Level

Field

Level 1

YY1_BUNDLEITEMNUM_BDI

Level 2

YY1_BUNDLEPRODDESC_BDI

 

6.3  Define the Formula (Trigger Condition)

App: Manage Your Solution → SSCUI 104023 (Define Formulas for Flexible Billing Output Aggregation – PS)

6.3.1 Create a formula and assign Set Aggregation Rule to 9

6.3.2 Create an entry in the Define Decision Table and add the Aggregation Rule 9

With this in place, the output form will automatically group billing items by bundle and present them hierarchically on the output document.

Step 7: Create custom form for adjusting aggregation for Solution Bundle in Output

This step to modify the form template is needed because the output example we have in this blog, should show the subitems of the bundle but not their prices. If prices of the subitems are to be displayed and only aggregation is required then this step would not be required. With step 6 execution, that would be achieved.

7.1  Download the form template to modify for use

App: Maintain Form Templates (F1434)

7.1.1  Download the standard template: SDBIL_CI_PROF_SRV_XX.

7.1.2  Open the .xdp file in Adobe LiveCycle Designer.

7.1.3  In the Data View, the three custom fields — YY1_BUNDLEITEMNUM_BDI, YY1_BUNDLEPRODID_BDI, YY1_BUNDLEPRODDESC_BDI — should be available for each item. Use them to enhance the item table in the form layout to aggregate by solution bundle but hide the prices of the subitems.

7.1.4  Save the modified file with a new name, e.g., Z_PROF_SRV_FORM_BUNDLE.xdp.

7.2  Upload the custom form and define output rules

App: Maintain Form Templates (F1434)

7.2.1  Upload Z_PROF_SRV_FORM_BUNDLE.xdp.

 

App: Output Parameter Determination(W0138)

7.2.2  Select Billing Document in Show Rules for and Form Template in Determination Step in Select Business Rules section.

7.2.3  Create an entry and assign the form template Z_PROF_SRV_FORM_BUNDLE to be used by the billing document to be created by solution order in the Maintain Business Rules section.   

 

How this looks in action

You would find the extension fields for the solution bundle in the list of the available fields which you access using the gear icon on the top right corner of the item table on the billing document. You can make them visible for the item table.

You will find the output entry for the billing document has the new form assigned to it. You can use the preview option to view it.

entry.title: What’s New in Identity and Access Management in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition
entry.content:
1.  Overview

Identity and Access Management (IAM) in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition provides the foundational security layer that controls user access to business applications and backend services. Traditionally, IAM apps were grouped into business catalogs, with authorization default values aggregated strictly at the catalog level. These business catalogs served as the essential building blocks for constructing business roles. The traditional authorization flow works as follows:

Business Role  →  Business Catalog  →  Fiori→  Authorization Defaults / Services

While this catalog-centric model provided a straightforward way to bundle related apps, it operated on an "all-or-nothing" principle. Assigning a catalog granted access to every application within it.

To solve these limitations, SAP evolved the IAM architecture from rigid catalog bundles to modular application entities.

2.  What Is "App as Entity"?

Starting with Release 2502, SAP introduced “App Authorization Variants” for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. An App Authorization Variant acts as a standalone wrapper around an application's authorization requirements, decoupling it from the catalog to make the individual IAM App -rather than the catalog- the smallest assignable unit of authorization.

With Release 2608, this capability expands into the broader "App as Entity" framework, enabling administrators to directly assign, toggle active/inactive, and manage application access with fine-grained precision when building Business Roles.

The diagram below illustrates this shift from broad catalog bundling to standalone, app-level role construction.

2.1  The Challenges of the Catalog-Only Approach

While catalogs provide great pre-bundled workplaces, relying solely on them introduced friction:

  • Inability to create business roles for a specific subset of apps without custom catalog creation.
  • High change-management effort when catalogs required splitting due to evolving requirements.
  • Automatic exposure of newly added apps to end-users upon upgrades, along with their underlying authorizations.

By shifting to "App as Entity," administrators can now assemble roles based on exact user tasks without rigid constraints, enabling the direct launch of all application types via assigned transaction codes in S/4HANA Public Edition and SAP BTP, ABAP environment.

2.2  Practical Scenarios:

  • User Management: Grant user access to the Business User app without exposing access to the Business Roles app.
  • Procurement: Assign access to a specific Purchase Order app without granting permissions to all applications inside the broader Procurement catalog.

3.  How App Assignment Works

"App as Entity" does not replace Business Catalogs. Instead, Business Catalogs and direct app selection run side-by-side in parallel.

When configuring a role in the Maintain Business Roles Fiori app (F1492), administrators now have two assignment mechanisms:

Assignment Type

How It Works

Best Used For

Assigned via Business Catalog

The Business Catalog is assigned to the Business Role. IAM Apps within that catalog can be selectively activated or deactivated and are part of the resulting role accordingly.

Standard role setup where a user needs the complete suite of applications in a functional area.

Direct Assignment

An App Authorization Variant /IAM App is selected directly for a Business Role without requiring the overarching Business Catalog to be assigned.

Granular role setup where a user needs only 1 or 2 specific applications from a larger domain.

3.1  In-App Granular Control

Beyond assigning broad Business Catalogs, administrators can now manage application access with pinpoint accuracy. The Maintain Business Roles app (F1492) allows security leads to directly add, remove, toggle, or inspect individual IAM Apps to match exact user job responsibilities.

3.1.1  Practical Example: Direct App Selection in Action

To see how "App as Entity" works in practice, consider configuring the "Internal Sales Representative" role as an example inside the Maintain Business Roles app.

As shown in the screenshot above, administrators are no longer limited to managing entire catalogs. Instead, the dedicated IAM Apps tab allows granular control over individual applications:

  • Direct App Authorization Variants: Specific apps, such as Display Business Partner, Display Customer (Centrally), or Supplier are assigned directly as "App Authorization Variants" with their linked transaction objects.
  • Selection & Activation Control: Checkboxes alongside each IAM App let administrators select specific items to Add, Remove, Activate, or Deactivate permissions without affecting the rest of the business domain.
  • Catalog-Free Flexibility: Notice that this role has 0 Business Catalogs assigned yet contains 27 IAM Apps assigned directly. This proves that roles can now be built using standalone app entities tailored to exact job tasks.

3.1.2  Toggling Apps ON/OFF

In addition to Direct Assignment, administrators can open an assigned Business Catalog inside the Maintain Business Roles app (F1492) and toggle individual IAM Apps ON or OFF.

 Important Note on Toggling:

Toggling an app OFF inside F1492 suppresses its underlying authorization defaults for that specific Business Role instance only. It does NOT alter or remove the app definition from the underlying Business Catalog in ABAP Development Tools (ADT), preserving the central catalog definition for other roles.


4.  Application Scope: SAP Standard vs. Customer-Developed Apps

The "App as Entity" model applies to both SAP-delivered content and custom-built extensions:

4.1  SAP Standard Applications

As introduced in Section 2, SAP delivers standard content pre-configured as individual App Authorization Variants (SIA6 objects).

For standard applications, this eliminates the need to assign full standard catalogs. Security administrators can directly select individual SAP standard apps when building Business Roles, ensuring users receive access only to the exact standard functionality required for their tasks while avoiding the overhead of creating custom catalogs in ADT.

4.2  Customer-Developed Applications (Developer Extensibility)

Custom applications built via ABAP Cloud / ADT using the ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model (RAP) are defined as External IAM Apps (SIA6 objects).

  • The Migration Requirement: To enable custom apps for individual selection in Business Roles, existing customer IAM Apps (SIA6) and their corresponding Business Catalogs (GBAK objects) must undergo a one-time migration using the built-in migration wizard in ABAP Development Tools (ADT).
  • The Outcome: Once migrated, customer-developed apps can participate in direct assignments and individual toggling just like SAP standard applications.


5  On-Premise (PFCG) to Cloud IAM Migration Realities

A common question during cloud transformation projects is whether existing On-Premise PFCG roles can be migrated directly into S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

5.1  Key Architectural Differences

Feature

On-Premise (PFCG)

S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (IAM)

Primary Building Block

Transactions (TCODES), Auth Objects, & Profiles

IAM Apps (SIA6), Business Catalogs, & Business Roles

Menu Maintenance

Direct TCode insertion in PFCG Menu tab

IAM Apps bundled in Business Catalogs via ADT

Authorization Abstraction

Direct maintenance of Auth Objects & Fields in SU24

Managed via IAM Apps, Business Catalogs, and Restriction Types

5.2  Migration Reality

Because On-Premise PFCG roles lack the underlying IAM App metadata layer (SIA6 objects), there is no automated 1-to-1 role import tool.

  • Best Practice: Customers migrating from On-Premise to S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition must construct their business roles using standard SAP reference catalogs or custom IAM Apps created in ADT.


6  Key Takeaways

  • Greater Flexibility: Security teams can build roles aligned with real user job descriptions using Direct Assignment or Catalog-based Assignment.
  • Reduced Customization: Eliminates the need to build redundant custom catalogs in ADT just to exclude a single application.
  • Segregation of Duties (SoD) Preserved: Business Catalogs remain the standard for grouping apps and preserving regularly audited SoD compliance. App as Entity adds fine-grained flexibility on top of this foundation.
  • Migration Needed for Custom Content: Existing customer-developed IAM Apps (SIA6) and catalogs (GBAK) must be migrated via the ADT wizard to participate in direct assignment.


7  More to read:

To dive deeper, explore the following official resources and reference guides:

  • Identity and Access Management (IAM)
  • Maintain Business Roles (Fiori App F1492)
  • Creating an IAM App for the Business Service
  • IAM Information System App (F2450) Usage Guide

entry.title: How to Delete a Stuck Service Entry Sheet in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud When Originated from SAP BN
entry.content:
Introduction

If you are running SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud integrated with SAP Business Network (formerly Ariba Network) via scope item 42K, you may have run into a frustrating scenario: a supplier submits a Service Entry Sheet (SES) through SAP Business Network, the SES lands in your S/4HANA system — but now, for whatever reason, it needs to be deleted. The PO quantity is blocked, no new SES can be raised against the same PO line, and neither the buyer team in S/4HANA nor the supplier in Business Network can find a way to remove it.

 

This blog post explains exactly why this happens, and gives you two concrete options to resolve it — from a simple configuration setting in Business Network, to a manual SOAP payload workaround for stubborn cases.

 

The Problem Scenario

Let's walk through a typical example that leads to this situation:

 

  1. Supplier creates a Service Entry Sheet in SAP Business Network against a Purchase Order.
  2. The SES syncs to S/4HANA Public Cloud via the managed integration gateway (Communication Arrangement SAP_COM_0237). The SES appears in the Manage Service Entry Sheets Fiori app with status Submitted / In Approval.
  3. The SES has NOT been approved yet — it is sitting in approval or was rejected at the buyer's end.
  4. Supplier realizes the SES was submitted by mistake — wrong quantity, wrong PO line, or created in error.
  5. Supplier looks for a Cancel button in Business Network — it does not exist. There is no cancel option visible to the supplier.
  6. Buyer tries to delete the SES directly in S/4HANA — the system blocks it. Because the SES was created from SAP Business Network, deletion must also originate from Business Network. S/4HANA will not allow a direct manual deletion.
  7. Result: PO line quantity is fully consumed by the stuck SES. No new SES can be created for the same PO line. The procurement process is stuck.

 

Note: This is standard SAP system design — the SES lifecycle is owned by the system that created it. Since SAP Business Network created the SES, the delete instruction must also come from Business Network into S/4HANA via the integration.

 

Root Cause

By default, SAP Business Network does not show a Cancel option to suppliers for Service Entry Sheets they have submitted. The setting that controls this behaviour is disabled out of the box and must be explicitly enabled by the buyer administrator.

 

Additionally, even when the setting is enabled, network delays or integration errors can sometimes cause the cancel request to not flow through to S/4HANA — leaving the SES in an orphaned state on the S/4HANA side.

 

Solution

There are two options available. Start with Option 1 — it is the cleaner, supported approach.

 

Option 1 — Enable 'Allow Suppliers to Cancel Service Sheets' in SAP Business Network   (Recommended)

This is the standard, supported way to resolve the issue. Once enabled, the supplier will see a Cancel button directly in SAP Business Network and can trigger the deletion themselves — the cancel request will flow automatically to S/4HANA via the integration.

 

Steps:

 

  1. Log in to SAP Business Network as the Buyer Administrator.
  2. Go to Company Settings (top-right menu → Company Settings).
  3. Navigate to Service Entry Sheet Settings.
  4. Find the parameter: "Allow suppliers to cancel service sheets that they create"
  5. Enable the setting and save.
  6. Inform the supplier to log back in to SAP Business Network — they will now see a Cancel button on the SES.
  7. Supplier clicks Cancel in Business Network → the delete message is sent automatically to S/4HANA → SES is removed → PO quantity is released.

 

When to use Option 1: Use this whenever possible. It is the clean, system-integrated approach. The cancel flows through the same SOAP interface that originally created the SES, and no manual intervention is needed on the S/4HANA side.

 

Option 2 — Manually Send the Delete Payload via Bruno / Postman

Use this option when:

  • Option 1 is already enabled but the supplier's cancel is stuck and not flowing to S/4HANA.
  • The integration is experiencing errors and the automatic delete message was lost.
  • You need an immediate resolution without waiting for Business Network to process the cancel.

 

This approach simulates what SAP Business Network would send — you manually construct and POST the SOAP delete message directly to the inbound web service in S/4HANA.

 

Step 1 — Get the Service URL from SAP_COM_0237

  1. Log in to SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud.
  2. Open the Communication Arrangements app (search in Fiori Launchpad).
  3. Find the arrangement for scope item 42K: SAP_COM_0237 (Ariba Network — Buyer Integration via SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway).
  4. Under Inbound Services, find: "Service Entry Sheet — Create, Delete (Lean Services)"
  5. Copy the Service URL — it will look like:
    https://<your-s4hana-host>/sap/bc/srt/scs_ext/sap/serviceentrysheetrequest_in

 

Step 2 — Get the Inbound Communication Credentials

  1. In the same Communication Arrangement (SAP_COM_0237), go to the Inbound Communication section.
  2. Copy the Communication User and its password.
  3. Note: This workaround applies when Basic Authentication is configured for the inbound service. If your arrangement uses certificate-based auth, configure your API client accordingly.

 

Step 3 — Construct and Send the Delete Payload

Configure your API client (Bruno / Postman / similar):

  • Method: POST
  • URL: Service URL from Step 1
  • Auth: Basic Auth — username/password from Step 2
  • Content-Type: text/xml
  • Add a WS-Addressing header: wsa:MessageID with value urn:uuid:<unique-uuid>

 

If you are using Bruno, add this Pre-Request script to auto-generate the UUID:

 

// Bruno Pre-Request Script
const { v4: uuidv4 } = require('uuid');
const messageId = 'urn:uuid:' + uuidv4();
bru.setVar('myMessageId', messageId);

 

Then reference it in the SOAP Header as: {{myMessageId}}

 

Below is a complete example delete payload with fully dummy values. Replace the highlighted fields with values from the original SES create payload (see the field reference table below):

 

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<soapenv:Envelope
    xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/"
    xmlns:wsa="http://www.w3.org/2005/08/addressing">

  <soapenv:Header>
    <wsa:MessageID>{{myMessageId}}</wsa:MessageID>
  </soapenv:Header>

  <soapenv:Body>
    <n0:ServiceEntrySheetRequestMsg
        xmlns:n0="http://sap.com/xi/SAPGlobal20/Global">

      <MessageHeader>
        <ID>SESTST-20261028-001</ID>
        <ReferenceID>SES-TEST-001</ReferenceID>
        <CreationDateTime>2026-10-01T10:00:00+03:00</CreationDateTime>
        <SenderBusinessSystemID>AN00000000001</SenderBusinessSystemID>
        <RecipientBusinessSystemID>XXXXXXXX</RecipientBusinessSystemID>
        <SenderParty>
          <InternalID>AN00000000002</InternalID>
        </SenderParty>
        <RecipientParty>
          <InternalID>AN00000000001</InternalID>
        </RecipientParty>
        <BusinessScope>
          <TypeCode> </TypeCode>
          <InstanceID schemeID=""> </InstanceID>
        </BusinessScope>
      </MessageHeader>

      <ServiceEntrySheetEntity>
        <ActionCode>03</ActionCode>
        <ApprovalStatus>20</ApprovalStatus>
        <DeleteInApproval>true</DeleteInApproval>
        <ServiceEntrySheet> </ServiceEntrySheet>
        <ServiceEntrySheetName>SES-TEST-001</ServiceEntrySheetName>
        <PurchaseOrder>4500000001</PurchaseOrder>
        <ResponsiblePerson> </ResponsiblePerson>

        <ServiceEntrySheetItemList>
          <ServiceEntrySheetItemEntity>
            <ActionCode>03</ActionCode>
            <ConfirmedQuantity unitCode="E51">1.0</ConfirmedQuantity>
            <NetPriceAmount currencyCode="USD">1000.0</NetPriceAmount>
            <PurchaseOrderItem>10</PurchaseOrderItem>
            <QuanitityUnit>E51</QuanitityUnit>
            <Service>8000000001</Service>
            <ServiceEntrySheetItem>1</ServiceEntrySheetItem>
            <ServiceEntrySheetItemReference>1</ServiceEntrySheetItemReference>
            <ServiceEntrySheetItemDesc>Sample Service Description</ServiceEntrySheetItemDesc>
            <ServicePerformanceDate>2026-10-01T12:00:00+03:00</ServicePerformanceDate>
            <ServicePerformanceEndDate>2026-10-05T12:00:00+03:00</ServicePerformanceEndDate>
            <WorkItem> </WorkItem>
          </ServiceEntrySheetItemEntity>
        </ServiceEntrySheetItemList>

      </ServiceEntrySheetEntity>
    </n0:ServiceEntrySheetRequestMsg>
  </soapenv:Body>
</soapenv:Envelope>

 

Important: Keep all MessageHeader fields (SenderBusinessSystemID, RecipientBusinessSystemID, SenderParty, RecipientParty, CreationDateTime) identical to the original create payload. The <ID> field must be a short unique identifier — max 35 characters. Do NOT put the full urn:uuid string in the <ID> field; the UUID belongs only in the wsa:MessageID SOAP header.

 

Field Reference — Where to Get Each Value

The original create payload can be found in the message monitoring in S/4HANA. Use the values from that payload unchanged - only the ActionCode and DeleteInApproval are different for the delete.

Verifying the Result

After sending the payload, confirm the delete was processed successfully:

 

  1. In S/4HANA: Open the Manage Service Entry Sheets Fiori app its status should show as Deleted.
  2. Check the PO: Open the PO in the Manage Purchase Orders app — the consumed/open quantity on the relevant PO line should be released.
  3. For errors: Monitor Messages (or use the AIF Monitor Fiori app) to check if the inbound message was processed successfully or if there is an error that needs to be resolved.

Quick Comparison: Option 1 vs Option 2

Related Information

  • Scope Item 42K — Automation of Source-to-Pay with SAP Business Network
  • Communication Arrangement SAP_COM_0237 — Ariba Network Buyer Integration via SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway
  • SAP Component: MM-PUR-GF-ES-2Cl (Service Entry Sheet)

 

Final Thoughts

A stuck Service Entry Sheet that originated from SAP Business Network is a frustrating but solvable problem. The root cause — the missing cancel option for suppliers — is a single configuration setting in Business Network that many buyers have not enabled. Turning it on resolves the issue permanently for all future cases.

 

For cases that are already stuck, the manual SOAP payload approach gives you full control to send the exact delete instruction that S/4HANA expects, using the same interface that SAP Business Network uses internally. The key is to take the values from the original create payload and change only the ActionCode to 03 and set DeleteInApproval to true.

 

Hope this helps someone who has been going in circles trying to figure out why the SES cannot be deleted! If you have questions or a different scenario, drop them in the comments below.

entry.title: S/4HANA Public Cloud Delivers Industry-Leading Upgrade Performance
entry.content:
What used to take more than eight hours now takes 13 minutes. With 2608 Release upgrade, SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud now completes production system upgrades in an average of 13 minutes, a 97% reduction from more than eight hours in 2019, validated consistently across more than 2,780 production systems worldwide. Non-production systems perform even better, averaging 7 minutes, bringing the overall landscape average to 10 minutes. This is not a theoretical benchmark. It is the measured, repeatable outcome of seven years of sustained engineering commitment.

The numbers tell the story clearly:

YearAverage Production DowntimeKey Driver
2019516 minutes (approximately 8.6 hours)Legacy in-place upgrade model
2021144 minutesIntroduction of Blue-Green architecture
2023Temporary increase35% expansion in customer base
202441 minutesContinuous optimization
202519 minutesParallel preparation maturity
202613 minutesCurrent benchmark


The breakthrough stems from a fundamental rethinking of how upgrades are delivered. Rather than taking a live system offline, SAP uses Blue Green deployment architecture, building an entirely new upgraded environment in parallel while customers continue working.
By the time the switchover begins, software installation, database schema updates, customization validation, and integration testing are already complete. The 13-minute window covers only the final data synchronization, traffic switchover, and application server restart.

Because 96% of upgrade work happens during the parallel preparation phase, customer-specific factors such as data volume, custom code complexity, and integration landscape do not extend downtime. Whether a customer has 100 GB or 10 TB of data, the switchover remains consistently brief. The complexity is handled during uptime, not during the maintenance window.

For businesses, this change is material. Manufacturing customers no longer require extended production shutdowns. Financial institutions maintain service level agreement uptime and minimize regulatory exposure. Global enterprises find coordination across time zones dramatically simpler. The predictability of 13-minute upgrades also makes the half yearly release cadence of SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud operationally viable, allowing customers to stay current with the latest innovations without disrupting Operations.

One distinction is worth noting when evaluating vendors. SAP reports actual measured downtime, defined as the time from when the last user transaction completes to when the first user can log back in, averaged across all production systems. This differs from scheduled maintenance windows, which represent calendar time that is blocked but may not reflect true system unavailability. Customers should ask whether a vendor's published figures represent reserved windows or actual downtime.

The shift from more than eight hours to 13 minutes is not simply an operational improvement. It is a change in what customers should expect from enterprise cloud enterprise resource planning. With a clear roadmap targeting fewer than five minutes and a longer-term vision of eliminating scheduled maintenance entirely.

SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud is setting a new standard. The question for customers is no longer how long upgrades will take, but when they will become completely invisible.

entry.title: Why You Should Migrate Cost Center Groups to Global Hierarchies
entry.content:
In an earlier release of SAP S4/HANA Cloud Public Edition, the Manage Global Hierarchies (ID: F2918) was introduced as a central place for maintaining various hierarchy types, including cost center hierarchies. One of its key purposes is to replace the legacy Manage Cost Center Groups app (ID: F1024).

We strongly recommend migrating your cost center groups to Manage Global Hierarchies to take advantage of its enhanced capabilities, ensure business continuity, and future-proof your processes.

In this blog, we’ll explore the benefits of the new app, compare it with the classic app, and guide you through the migration process.

The Traditional Way: Manage Cost Center Groups

For years, cost center groups were created and edited in the classic app Manage Cost Center Groups. Cost center standard hierarchy could also be edited there.  

The following graphic provides an overview of the app user interface:

To use a cost center group in reporting, the following steps are required after creating or editing the group:
Step 1: Mark the hierarchy as report-relevant
Open the Set Report Relevancy app (ID: F5295) and mark the hierarchy as report-relevant.
Step 2: Replicate the hierarchy
Use the Replicate Runtime Hierarchy (ID: F1478) app to replicate set-based hierarchies to back-end database tables. If this replication is not performed, then these hierarchies cannot be used in reporting.

For more information, refer to the following documentation on the SAP Help Portal:

  • Manage Cost Center Groups (Deprecated)
  • Set Report Relevancy
  • Replicate Runtime Hierarchy 

The New Way: Manage Global Hierarchies

The Manage Global Hierarchies app introduced in a recent release, modernizes cost center hierarchy maintenance. Aside from viewing, creating, and editing cost center hierarchies as in the classic app, the new app enables you to quickly create hierarchies by importing or copying from existing hierarchies in the event of structure changes or changing reporting needs. Additionally, you can check change logs and maintain node texts in multiple languages for applicable hierarchy types. 

Key Features

  • View and filter existing hierarchies by criteria such as hierarchy type, status, and validity timeframe
  • Create, copy, edit hierarchies, and manage their validity timeframes
  • Activate or deactivate hierarchies for runtime use
  • Export, edit, and import hierarchies via a spreadsheet
  • Import hierarchies created with compatible applications
  • View change logs of applicable hierarchy types
  • Maintain node texts in multiple languages for applicable hierarchy types
  • After being activated, hierarchies can be consumed in all analytical reports
  • Reuse Hierarchies in Group-Related Apps

The following graphic provides an overview of the app user interface:

For more information, refer to Manage Global Hierarchies  on the SAP Help Portal.  

Why Migrate?

Compared with the Manage Cost Center Groups app, which is used to maintain set-based groups, Manage Global Hierarchies provides a unified solution for managing various hierarchy types within a single application. In addition, thanks to the SAP Fiori UI technology, hierarchies can be exported to, edited in, and imported from spreadsheets, significantly improving maintenance efficiency. Furthermore, the global hierarchy framework simplifies the consumption of hierarchies across analytical applications and reports, enabling more consistent and seamless reporting experiences.

We strongly recommend using the new Manage Global Hierarchies app to maintain cost centers. Rest assured, existing cost center groups created in the classic app can be seamlessly migrated to the global hierarchies framework. We encourage you to do the migration as soon as possible for the following reasons:

  • The new app provides more robust functionality and greater flexibility to meet your business needs that are unavailable in the classic app.
  • The classic app is planned to be deprecated in the future.
  • New features are only delivered to the new app.

For more information, refer to Set-Based Groups versus Global Hierarchies. 

How to Migrate: Step-by-Step

Migrating your existing cost center groups is simple and efficient. Follow the steps below using the Migrate Set-Based Groups to Global Hierarchies app (ID: F6228) . 

1. Open the app, choose Hierarchy Type 0101 (Cost Center Group).

2. Select the old hierarchy of the cost center group you’d like to migrate, and choose the Migrate button. Take 8765 as an example.

3. In the migration details page, choose Migrate. 

4. You will then be navigated to the page below, which confirms that the hierarchy has been migrated to the Manage Global Hierarchies app.

5. To confirm the migration, open the Manage Global Hierarchies app and check the details of 8765.

6. Repeat the steps above to migrate all cost center groups.

After completing the migration, click the Mark as Completed button in the aforementioned migration app to finalize the process and confirm that the cost center type has been successfully and fully migrated.

For more information, refer to the following documentation: How to Migrate Cost Center Groups to Global Hierarchies 

Special Case: Cost Center Standard Hierarchy

Among all cost center hierarchies, the Cost Center Standard Hierarchy (Hierarchy ID 1) has special behavior:
• Hierarchy ID 1 is reserved for the standard hierarchy. All cost centers are automatically assigned to this hierarchy upon creation.
• The Standard Hierarchy Node field in the Manage Cost Centers app is bidirectionally synchronized with the structure maintained in Manage Global Hierarchies.
• Because all cost centers are automatically assigned upon creation, the Unassigned tab is always empty for Hierarchy ID 1.
Note: Before activating cost center standard hierarchy 1, ensure that all cost centers have been assigned to it. Failure to do so will prevent the activation of the standard hierarchy. If you encounter this issue, check the Unassigned tab. If there are any cost centers listed, assign them to the standard hierarchy.

For more information, see Cost Center Standard Hierarchies on the SAP Help Portal.  

Final Thoughts

The Manage Global Hierarchies app offers enhanced functionality and eliminates the need for separate report relevancy and replication steps before cost center hierarchies can be used for reporting. As the Manage Cost Center Groups app has been deprecated, migrating your cost center groups to Manage Global Hierarchies helps ensure business continuity while enabling you to take advantage of its new capabilities.

We hope this blog has helped you better understand the transition process. If you have any questions or need further assistance, feel free to leave a comment below.

entry.title: 如何在 SAP Cloud ERP 中为迁移对象添加字段
entry.content:
在将数据迁移到 SAP S/4HANA Cloud 的过程中，标准迁移对象有时无法完全覆盖企业的个性化需求——例如，某些字段并未默认包含在 SAP S/4HANA Migration Cockpit 的 XML 或 CSV 模板中。 此时，可以借助 「Model Your Migration」（SAP S/4HANA Migration Object Modeler）应用，手动将所需字段添加到迁移对象中。 本文将以 供应商（Supplier） 对象为例，带您一步步完成操作。

         ⚠️ 注意：本文内容仅适用于使用 「通过暂存表迁移数据（Migrate Data Using Staging Tables）」 方式的场景。

前提条件

  • 具有访问 SAP Fiori 应用「Model Your Migration Objects」的权限
  • 已分配所需角色：SAP_BR_ADMINISTRATOR
  • 使用的迁移方式为「通过暂存表迁移数据（Migrate Data Using Staging Tables）」
  • 确认您希望添加的字段已被允许使用（请参阅对应 SAP Note，例如 SAP Note 3019787 中关于 Supplier 的说明）。 本示例中，我们将把字段 CONTACTALLOWANCECTRCENBP 添加到供应商迁移对象。
  • 所有支持的迁移对象汇总说明，请参阅 SAP Note 2999428。

操作步骤：以供应商迁移对象为例

目标：将字段 CONTACTALLOWANCECTRCENBP 添加到供应商（Supplier）迁移对象中。

1. 打开 Migration Object Modeler 应用

启动 SAP Fiori 应用「Model Your Migration Objects」，并进入您的迁移项目。

首次打开时，系统会提示：该应用仅支持查看和编辑使用「通过暂存表迁移数据」方式的迁移项目和对象。 如需查看使用「直接从 SAP 系统迁移数据（Migrate Data Directly from SAP system）」方式的对象，请通过「实施活动（Implementation Activities）」应用访问 SAP S/4HANA Migration Object Modeler。

 

2. 找到供应商迁移对象

展开迁移对象节点，查看所有对象列表，然后双击「Supplier（供应商）」将其打开。

 

3. 查看源结构（Source Structures）

双击「Source Structures」。 如果界面上看不到技术名称，请点击 Settings（设置） 并开启技术名称显示。

 

 

4. 切换至编辑模式

将应用切换至 Edit（编辑） 模式，以允许对迁移对象进行修改。

 

5. 添加新字段

选择相关的源结构，点击「Add Field（添加字段）」。 输入新字段的详细信息（例如 ZZ_NEW_FIELD）；系统会将其标记为自定义字段。

在本示例中，我们需要添加字段 CONTACTALLOWANCECTRCENBP。

 

 

6. 保存更改

保存您的输入。如有需要，可使用「Full Screen on/off」按钮切换视图。

 

7. 映射新字段（Field Mapping）

双击「Field Mapping」（确认仍处于编辑模式）。 在源结构中搜索您刚添加的字段，以及目标侧的对应字段（如 CONTACTALLOWANCECTRCENBP）。

将源字段拖拽到目标字段上完成映射，或者右键点击并选择「Assign Rule（分配规则）」。

 

 

8. 验证并保存映射

仔细检查映射关系是否正确，然后保存更改。

 

9. 同步结构（Synchronize Structures）

执行结构同步，以使您的更改生效。确认弹出的提示框，然后退出应用。

 

10. 在 SAP S/4HANA Migration Cockpit 中验证

返回「Migrate Your Data – Migration Cockpit」，检查您的迁移项目，查看暂存表状态。

  • 如果表状态显示为 「Adjustment Required」，请选中该表并点击「Adjust Structure」。
  • 如果在 Model Your Migration 应用中已完成同步，状态应直接显示为 「OK」。

 

11. 在模板文件中确认字段

新添加的字段现在将出现在迁移对象对应的 XML 模板文件中，可供数据填充使用。

 

补充说明

  • 重置迁移对象： 如有需要，可将迁移对象重置为 SAP 原始模板版本。注意：此操作会移除所有自定义更改。
  • 更新迁移对象： SAP 会定期更新迁移对象。当系统提示更新时，建议及时更新，以确保与最新版本的兼容性。
  • 收藏夹功能： 可将常用的迁移项目或对象添加至收藏夹，方便快速访问（每类最多支持 10 个）。

entry.title: Company Code Assignments to Profit Centers — From Individual Maintenance to Mass Processing
entry.content:
Understanding Company Code Assignments in Profit Centers

Before exploring the new functionality, it is worth understanding how the assignment logic itself works — particularly the distinction between default and explicit assignments.

Default Assignment

When a new Profit Center is created, the system automatically considers all Company Codes as assigned to that Profit Center. No manual configuration is required. The Profit Center is simply available across all Company Codes by default.

Explicit Assignment

Users can also manually define which Company Codes are assigned to a Profit Center. Once explicit assignments are maintained, the default logic no longer applies. The Profit Center is then assigned only to the Company Codes that have been explicitly selected.

This distinction has a practical consequence when a new Company Code is created.

What Happens When a New Company Code Is Created?

When a new Company Code is created, it automatically becomes visible on detail page in the Company Code section (in Manage Profit Centers app (New version - F3516A)) of all Profit Centers. However, visibility and assignment status are not the same thing.

  • For Profit Centers using default assignment logic, the new Company Code is automatically considered assigned. No action is required.
  • For Profit Centers with explicit assignments, the new Company Code appears as unassigned. Users must explicitly assign it if the Profit Center should be available for that Company Code.

This behavior is consistent and predictable, but it requires attention — particularly in organizations where Profit Centers have been individually configured with explicit assignments over time.

 

SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition Context
In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, a single Controlling Area is used: A000. This means all Profit Centers and all Company Codes in your system belong to the same Controlling Area. The assignment logic described above applies uniformly across all Profit Centers in the system. 

 

1 by 1 Individual Company Code Assignment

The current versions (old and new) of the Manage Profit Centers app already allows users to manage Company Code assignments at the individual Profit Center level. After opening detail page of Profit Center, users can assign additional Company Codes or remove existing assignments as needed.

This approach works well when changes are limited to one or a few Profit Centers. However, when changes need to be applied across a larger set of Profit Centers (for example, after a new Company Code has been created and must be explicitly assigned to hundreds of Profit Centers) individual maintenance quickly becomes impractical.

This is precisely the gap that the new release 2602 enhancement addresses.

Mass Company Code Assignment

With release 2602, users can assign and unassign Company Codes across multiple Profit Centers in a single operation. The functionality is accessible directly from the List Report Page of the Manage Profit Centers app (New version - F3516A) via the Assign Company Codes button.

The process follows 3 easy steps: downloading a template, modifying it in spreadsheet, and importing the changes into the system.

 

Step 1 — Download the Template

From the Manage Profit Centers (New version - F3516A) List Report Page, select via checkboxes the Profit Centers you want to include in the mass change. Click the Assign Company Codes button to initiate the process, then download the predefined Excel template.

The downloaded template reflects the selected Profit Centers and the Company Codes available in your system. It presents them in a matrix structure (Profit Centers in rows, Company Codes in columns) giving you a clear overview of the current assignment state before making any changes.

 

Step 2 — Modify and Upload the Template

The assignment logic in the template is straightforward: an X in a cell means the Company Code is assigned to the corresponding Profit Center. An empty cell means it is not assigned.

To assign a Company Code to a Profit Center, enter an X in the relevant cell. To remove an existing assignment, clear the cell. There is no need to enter identifiers manually or navigate system screens — the matrix is the working document.

 

 

One of the practical advantages of this approach is that users can apply standard Excel functionality to handle mass changes efficiently. Copying and pasting values across multiple cells, using the fill handle to extend assignments across rows or columns — all of these are available without any special configuration.

 

Once the required changes have been made, upload the modified file back into the application. An initial validation runs automatically during the upload to identify any spreadsheet issues before processing begins.

Step 3 — Import Changes

After a successful upload and initial validation, users can proceed to the import step. The system processes the requested Company Code assignments and unassignments across all selected Profit Centers and applies the changes to the Profit Center master data.

Application Log and Processing Monitoring

After the import, users can review the results in the Display Profit Center Logs (F9149). The log records the outcome of the mass processing operation, including "happy path" as well as any errors encountered during processing.

The Application Log provides transparency and traceability — users can see what was processed, identify any issues, and understand the overall outcome and verify results.

Key Benefits

  • The new mass assignment and unassignment capability in release 2602 delivers tangible improvements for day-to-day Profit Center administration.
  • Efficiency. Company Code assignments across multiple Profit Centers can be managed in a single operation, replacing a process that previously required opening and editing each Profit Center individually.
  • Reduced manual effort. Changes that previously required extensive screen navigation can now be prepared in spreadsheet and imported in 3 easy steps — a significant time saving when working with larger Profit Center structures.
  • Spreadsheet flexibility. Users can leverage the spreadsheet functions they already know (copy, paste, fill handle) to prepare mass changes quickly and accurately.
  • Data consistency. Built-in validations catch invalid configurations before they reach the system, protecting Profit Center master data from incomplete or incorrect assignments.
  • Transparency. The Application Log ensures that users can review processing results and identify any issues without guesswork.

 

Summary

Company Code assignment management in Profit Centers involves more nuance than it might initially appear — particularly the distinction between default and explicit assignment logic, and its implications when new Company Codes are created. The individual assignment management already available in the Manage Profit Centers application handles straightforward cases well. For organizations that need to maintain assignments across a larger set of Profit Centers, the mass assignment and unassignment functionality introduced in release 2602 provides a practical, spreadsheet-based solution with built-in validation and transparent processing results.
